name: Start-up Denmark

requirements.blocker_text: The business idea must be approved by an expert panel appointed by the Danish Business Authority (Erhvervsstyrelsen) before SIRI will accept a residence and work permit application -- the panel assesses whether the venture is genuinely innovative and capable of contributing growth and new jobs in Denmark.
requirements.fix_path: Submit a business plan to the Erhvervsstyrelsen expert panel and obtain approval before applying to SIRI.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires actively running the approved business as a self-employed person; the permit is limited to operating that specific business, and any material change to the business, or its closure, requires a fresh application.

evidence_required.document: Business plan submitted to the Erhvervsstyrelsen expert panel
Proof of funds to support the applicant and, at renewal, a fresh expert-panel reassessment of the business

outcome.duration_length: 2 years initially, renewable in further 3-year increments provided the business remains active and the expert panel reconfirms it meets requirements

sources.title: Nyidanmark.dk (SIRI) -- Start-up Denmark, official scheme page confirming the expert-panel approval requirement, team-of-up-to-3 structure, and duration terms

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: Start-up Denmark can be used not only for brand-new ventures but also to continue an existing self-employed business the applicant already established while resident in Denmark on a different basis, or to run a Danish branch of a foreign-based sole proprietorship -- three distinct use cases under one scheme, confirmed directly via nyidanmark.dk. The scheme explicitly supports teams: up to 3 people can apply together around a single shared business plan, a genuinely collaborative structure not commonly seen in this dataset's other work_independent routes (most, like Poland's D-8-4/OASIS or Italy's self-employment visa, are single-applicant). The permit is tightly scoped to the specific approved business -- a material change to the business plan or its closure requires an entirely new application and fresh expert-panel approval, and renewal itself requires the Erhvervsstyrelsen panel to reassess and reconfirm the business still meets requirements, a real, recurring approval gate not present in most comparable countries' investor/founder routes in this dataset, which typically only re-check financial thresholds at renewal rather than re-approving the underlying business concept. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use the general 4-year/8-year Danish tracks (see dk_permanent_residence); no accelerated path specific to Start-up Denmark participants was found in sources checked for this build.
